topic: product fitment and compatibility mistakes when buying parts and accessories
blind_spots: There is little direct buyer testimony describing the purchase, installation, return, and resolution process.
The evidence does not compare the accuracy of specific marketplaces, fitment standards, catalog providers, or compatibility tools.
There is no evidence establishing which interventions measurably reduce wrong-part purchases.
The evidence does not quantify the overall frequency of fitment errors, return rates specifically caused by incompatibility, or total financial impact.
Most evidence concerns automotive parts; there is little substantive evidence about fitment mistakes in other accessory categories.
contradictions: Some evidence attributes errors to inaccurate or incomplete seller compatibility data, while other evidence says customers select the wrong trim or engine type.
One seller attributes poor performance to broad advertising rather than the product page, whereas other sources identify unclear product pages and listings as central causes.
The Amazon return-rate claim says returns can be unrelated to product quality, but it does not establish that those returns are caused by fitment mistakes.
